question: Should nix-openclaw ship an interim documented push-model setup now, or wait for the draft Gmail pull-model contract before adding a first-class module interface?
rationale: The current workaround is functional, but the linked RFC and two upstream implementation pull requests propose a different long-term ingestion and supervision model; choosing the public Nix interface before that direction settles could create avoidable breaking churn.

options.title: Finish pull model first
options.body: Keep this issue as the nix-openclaw integration tracker and implement the first-class interface after the RFC and upstream worker contract are accepted and available.

options.title: Document push setup now
options.body: Add a narrow README or template section for the existing watcher, including `allowRequestSessionKey`, while deferring any new module options until the pull model stabilizes.

recommendation.title: Finish pull model first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the nix-openclaw integration tracker and implement the first-class interface after the RFC and upstream worker contract are accepted and available.

likelyOwner.reason: They are coordinating the RFC, gogcli implementation, OpenClaw supervision work, and promised nix-openclaw follow-up in the issue discussion.
